title: Dequant shadow allocator and token-aware kernel routing for low-overhead INT8/FP8 paths
creator: Liam Ortega
description: Context: dequantization overhead is a persistent contributor to decode latency in mixed-precision paths (INT8/FP8). Current runtime performs eager dequant into working tensors inside the main execution arena which causes extra copies, memory pressure on prefill, and contention during decode when KV cache hits are high. This ticket proposes a lightweight 'dequant shadow allocator' + token-aware routing policy so we can minimize copies, enable zero-copy decode in common cases, and make kernel selection decisions that include per-request sequence-length and cache-warmth heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Microbenchmark: reduce per-token dequant copy costs by >=40% for 2048-context GPT-like models on A100 baseline compared to current master
End-to-end: median decode latency for 8-token responses with cold KV cache improves by >=8% on INT8 path (95th percentile should not regress >5%)
Memory: peak working set during large-batch prefill reduces by at least 6% in representative workload (batch sizes 8-32, seq len distribution matching production traces)
No functional regressions: numeric outputs match INT8/FP8 reference within existing tolerances; unit tests for kernel fallbacks added
Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag and can be disabled per-customer route; automatic fallback to existing dequant path on assertion failures
